## Upstream changes 4.9.11 -> 4.9.12

**Verdict:** SAFE TO APPLY — a one-line security fix with no breaking changes, no variable changes, and no companion-service version requirement introduced.

### Breaking changes
- none found in the notes

### Variables
- none. No renamed, removed, or newly required variables. Note that the compose file's `x-images` default and the `.env.example` comment (`DASHY_IMAGE_VERSION=4.9.11`) both still reference the old version — bumping to 4.9.12 requires editing the compose file's `x-images` default (or setting `DASHY_IMAGE_VERSION=4.9.12` in `.env`), but that's a mechanical pin update, not a variable change introduced by the release.

### Data and dependencies
- none. No database, cache, or search engine version requirements appear in the notes, and the compose file pins no such companion service for this image.

### Before applying
- Update the pin: either bump `DASHY_IMAGE_VERSION` default in the compose file's `x-images` block to `4.9.12` (with the correct new digest), or set `DASHY_IMAGE_VERSION=4.9.12` in `.env` to override.
- No backup, migration, or config edit is required. The fix is described as: "🔐 Security fix for auth headers sent to lookalike origins" — worth applying promptly since it's a security fix, but it requires no operator action beyond the version bump.

### Notes read
- Compare-API commit log between `4.9.11` and `4.9.12` tags on `Lissy93/dashy` (3 commits) — no dedicated GitHub release notes exist for either tag, so the commit messages are the only record available.
- No UPGRADING, BREAKING_CHANGES, or CHANGELOG section was supplied for this range; none to weigh against the commit log.

## Upstream changes 28.2.0 -> 28.3.0

**Verdict:** SAFE TO APPLY — the notes contain only bug fixes, performance work and minor enhancements; the image's user/entrypoint/command/ports/volumes/healthcheck/environment are unchanged, and no companion service version requirement is introduced.

### Breaking changes
- none found in the notes

### Variables
- none — no new, renamed or removed variables are indicated by the notes, and `WHAT THE IMAGES THEMSELVES DIFFER IN` confirms the environment is unchanged between the two image builds.

### Data and dependencies
- none introduced by this range. One item is worth restating as already true, not as a change: the compose file's comment and `GITEA__actions__RUN_RETENTION_DAYS` default note that "Gitea 28 deletes completed runs older than RUN_RETENTION_DAYS at midnight, and upstream defaults it to 400" — this behaviour dates to the Gitea 28 line generally (already in effect at 28.2.0) and is explicitly worked around by the template's own default of `0`. It is not something this 28.2.0 → 28.3.0 upgrade changes or raises.
- The one security-relevant dependency bump in the notes — "*(deps)* Update module golang.org/x/net to v0.62.0 [security] (#40050) (#40051)" — is a vendored Go module inside the gitea binary, not an external service the compose file pins (postgres, traefik). No companion-service version is named by the notes, so the "NEEDS ATTENTION on unpinned companion version" rule does not apply here.

### Before applying
- No manual migration, backup-beyond-routine, or config edit is required by these notes. Standard practice still applies: let the existing `backups` service produce a fresh pg_dump/data tarball before pulling the new tag, then update `GITEA_IMAGE_VERSION` (or the `gitea` pin in `x-images`) and redeploy.

### Notes read
- v28.3.0 (2026-11-01) — the release being moved to
- v28.2.0 (2026-10-18) — the baseline release currently running, read only to confirm nothing in it is miscast as a change in this range

## Upstream changes 2.5.315 -> 3.0.1

**Verdict:** DO NOT APPLY UNATTENDED — this is a 2.x-to-3.x major jump with a mandatory, irreversible migration path, a raised PostgreSQL minimum the compose file does not cover, and a changed container command/volume layout.

This is not a routine patch bump. The 2.x line is end-of-life (`2.x releases have moved to https://github.com/requarks/wiki-v2` — baseline note) and 3.0 is a ground-up rewrite with a one-way import process, not an in-place upgrade.

### Breaking changes
- Wiki.js 3.0 requires importing content from a 2.x instance rather than upgrading in place; the notes repeatedly reference "import from wiki.js v2 utility" (`3.0.0-beta.605`) and multiple fixes to that import path (`rewrite 2.x paths to 3.x paths during import`, `reduce batch size for importing pages from 2.x`, `disable ky timeout during 2.x import calls`, `import from v2 locale mapping for pages / assets`). There is no documented direct in-place database upgrade for 2.5.x → 3.0.x in these notes.
- `beta.672`: *"API keys using page rules + remove X-API-Key header + make pg 17 the minimum"* — PostgreSQL 17 is required. The compose file already pins `postgres:17.11`, so this specific requirement is already satisfied — but see Data and dependencies below for a point this doesn't cover.
- `beta.639`: `encode paths to hex in ltrees to support non-latin chars` — internal path storage format changed; relevant if any 2.x data is carried over via import.
- Paths changed: the image's own volume layout gained a second mount, `/wiki/data/repo`, alongside the existing `/wiki/data/content` (see registry diff below) — not mentioned in the release notes at all, but it is real and the compose file does not mount it.
- Container start command changed from `node --no-deprecation server` to `node --no-experimental-webstorage backend`, and the entrypoint changed from `docker-entrypoint.sh` to `tini -s --`. This is an application-boot change the notes never mention; whether the image's internal entrypoint script still performs first-run setup is not documented here.
- `3.0.0-beta.705`: *"improve handling of PORT and WIKI_PORT env vars"* — behaviour around the port variables changed; the compose healthcheck and Traefik routing both hard-code port 3000, so confirm the container still listens there after upgrade.

### Variables
- `YARN_VERSION` removed from the image (was `1.22.22`) — not a compose/.env variable, informational only, no action.
- `NODE_VERSION` changed 24.21.0 → 26.13.0 inside the image — informational, not operator-set.
- New image-internal env defaults appear: `NODE_ENV=production`, `PUPPETEER_CACHE_DIR=/wiki/.cache/puppeteer`, `PUPPETEER_CHROME_SKIP_DOWNLOAD=true`. None of these are referenced in the compose file or `.env.example`; they are internal defaults, not currently overridden, no action required unless Puppeteer-based features (e.g. the new image editor / rendering, `f82f013`) are needed and the host wants to change caching behaviour.
- `.env.example` and the compose `x-images` block still show `WIKIJS_IMAGE_VERSION=2.5.315`; moving to `3.0.1` requires updating that pin (`WIKIJS_IMAGE_VERSION=3.0.1` or the digest form) — this is the actual mechanism of the upgrade in this template, not an upstream-named variable change.

### Data and dependencies
- Already true at 2.5.315, not introduced by this range: nothing in the 2.5.315 baseline notes states a Postgres minimum.
- Introduced by this range: `beta.672` states *"make pg 17 the minimum"*. The compose file pins `postgres:17.11`, which satisfies this — flag as verified, not a gap.
- The image's own volumes differ: registry shows a new required-looking mount `/wiki/data/repo` added in 3.0.1 that did not exist in 2.5.315 (`/wiki/data/content` only). The compose file only defines `wikijs-postgres` and backup volumes for the database tier; it has **no named volume for either `/wiki/data/content` or `/wiki/data/repo`** on the `wikijs` service today, meaning content/git-repo data inside the container is currently ephemeral at both versions — this predates the upgrade but becomes more consequential now that a second data path exists that notes don't document at all. Treat any content currently relying on container-internal storage as being at risk of loss on container replacement.
- Import from a 2.x dataset is described across multiple beta notes as batched, locale-aware, and path-rewriting — meaning it is a one-way, non-trivial data transformation, not a schema migration script bundled invisibly into startup.
- `55dd604`: *"run database sessions in UTC so timestamps aren't shifted"* — a behavioural/data change to how session timestamps are stored; relevant to anything reading raw DB timestamps.
- `b868bf7`: *"encode paths to hex in ltrees to support non-latin chars"* — ltree-based path storage encoding changed; relevant to raw SQL tooling against the Postgres database.

### Before applying
- Take a full backup of the `wikijs-postgres` volume and of any content/assets currently stored in the container (the `/wiki/data/content` and, as of 3.0.1, `/wiki/data/repo` paths), since the compose file does not currently persist either via a named volume.
- Do not upgrade the running container in place. Read the official upgrade documentation (`https://docs.js.wiki/setup/upgrade`) and the import procedure (`https://docs.js.wiki/setup/installation`, `https://js.wiki/blog/2026-wiki-js-3-release/`) referenced in the 3.0.1 notes before touching production — this template's compose file assumes a drop-in image swap, which is not what upstream describes for this range.
- Stand up 3.0.1 against a separate/test database first and run the "import from wiki.js v2" utility against a copy of the data, verifying page paths, locales, and non-Latin-character paths render correctly before pointing it at production data.
- Confirm Postgres is at 17.11 as already pinned (satisfies the beta.672 "pg 17 minimum") — no change needed here, just confirm before cutover.
- After updating `WIKIJS_IMAGE_VERSION` (or the full `WIKIJS_IMAGE_TAG`) to 3.0.1, verify the container still serves on port 3000 given the `PORT`/`WIKI_PORT` handling change, since both the Traefik label and the healthcheck hard-code that port.
- Check whether the container needs an explicit volume for `/wiki/data/repo` now that the image declares it; if git-based storage or any persistent repo data is used, add a named volume for it before switching versions.

### Notes read
- `requarks/wiki` release notes for `3.0.1`, `3.0.0-beta.705`, `3.0.0-beta.685`, `3.0.0-beta.672`, `3.0.0-beta.661`, `3.0.0-beta.651`, `3.0.0-beta.639`, `3.0.0-beta.628`, `3.0.0-beta.617`, `3.0.0-beta.605` (the full range covering this upgrade).
- Baseline note read: `v2.5.315`.
- No UPGRADING, BREAKING_CHANGES or CHANGELOG document was supplied separately from the release notes; none could be consulted beyond what's quoted above.
